title: The Nature of Divine Providential Correction
english: To understand this concerning men, about whom the divine teaching says: 'And he has kept those angels who did not observe their own rank in darkness.' And he says that men dwell in houses of clay instead of the material things, saying more simply that men were composed of the same clay. For not even the soul is of clay; for the body has been said to be clay.

'He struck them in the manner of a threshing floor.' This indicates the punishments sent against them as being insignificant. This is shown in Wisdom 11. But also the prophet says: 'The ruler asks, and the judge spoke peaceful words; it is the incense of his soul. And I will bring out their good things like a grain being threshed and walking according to a rule in a day of scrutiny' (Job 36:1-3), which is indicated by the continuous and sudden nature of the punishments and that which is sifted. For this indicates a rule. For if not 'he brings wrath day by day,' but 'he gives to each according to his works,' he makes this a rule instead of mixing it with goodness.

'Because they were not able to help themselves, they perished. For he breathed into them and they were dried up; they perished because they did not have wisdom.' Holding to the same principle, according to which she thinks that events happen through sin, and she says these things also. Since they were not able to help themselves through virtue after recognizing the evils, the afflictions followed them. And this she places under understanding: being unable to repel the severity of what came upon them through weakness, they perished, demonstrating the insignificance of human power.

This indeed and what follows seems to signify: 'For he breathed into them and they were dried up.' For it indicates that an overwhelming onslaught was not necessary against them, but only the breathing, which sufficed for their destruction, which he called loss. And from the same failing intellect follows: 'They perished because they did not have wisdom,' unaware that many wise men are afflicted...

They cast about. 'And call out, if anyone will obey you, or if you see any of the holy angels.' It seems as if he is providing an exhortation leading the holy one toward repentance, so that having come for the purpose of entreaty, he might happen to find one who assists and listens. And he also presents the phrase, 'or if you see any of the holy angels,' as being aware that they are not holy angels. For if he did not know this, the addition would be superfluous; it is as if he is distinguishing a holy [one] from a non-such. But those who say [he is mocking] claim that he says this ironically.

Regarding the beginning, he speaks again of the error, saying that through sin [10-15] so that he may know [15-20], 'for anger refutes the fool, and jealousy strikes the fallen one to death' (Proverbs 24:22). Thus it is to be read. [The text is heavily corrupted/gapped here] such as those who are displeasing to the providence of God. Why then do I myself fall into such calamities [8-12] and [lose] honor [6-10] according to what is said: 'Do not rejoice when your enemies rejoice, nor let your heart be glad when they stumble' (Proverbs 24:17), or 'jealousy [of] those who do lawlessness' (Proverbs 27:4). Jealousy is like it. And a second retribution [2-6] is [added] to the first [5-10], even if in irony. The phrase 'And call out, if anyone will obey you' will seem to have been spoken naturally, as if no one obeyed. [The text is gapped] as has been said.

'But I have seen fools casting seed, but immediately their harvest was ruined.' [The text is gapped] the mind under the roots... [the text is heavily corrupted/gapped here]... a many-rooted [thing] holds... and he speaks of human [things] happening, for immediately their harvest was ruined. To a great extent... [the text is gapped]... and the rich to be changed into poverty many times. But [it is not] to be praised for what is surrounding [it], but rather for the... [the text is gapped]... of this living... the [nature] of such arrogance, for the divine letter [is]...
